Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

2.1 The thread for stitchFng of gloves shall be polyamide/cotton core spun having the following 
requirements: 

Tkt — 50 

Nominal count and construction — Nm 50/2, Z/Finishing twist 

Finish — Glace 

Single thread breaking load — 2' 6 kg 

3. Dimensions — Covered in Fig. 1 are optional and figure is for guidance only. 

4. The softness of the leather used for gloves shall be measured by suitable instrument, such as 
tensometer by applying a load of 70 gm/cm parallel to the backbone to check the temporary elongation 
when tested. The temporary elongation shall be as follows: 

Butt portion of the leather used — 25 percent minimum 
Shoulder portion of the leather used — 25 to 30 percent 
Belly portion of the leather used — 40 to 45 percent

FIG. 1 WICKET KEEPING GLOVES 



5. Requirements — Wicket keeping gloves snail be well made and one each for right and left hand. 
The finger joints shall be such as to allow the player freedom of movement of the fingers. Between 
the thumb and the fore-finger,- a leather joining web shall be provided. The front cuff portion shall 
be padded with cotton and cane and sponge rubber bar or pad shall be provided across the wrist. At 
the back of the cuff portion, a strap and buckle or elastic band shall be provided to keep the gloves 
tight on the wrist. Inside the fingers, suitable sponge rubber tips shall be securely gummed, ihe 
stitching shall be strong and the general workmanship shall be of good quality. The gloves shall be 
comfortable to wear and the palm portion shall be padded with cotton or sponge rubber and made 
hollow so as to provide good catch when receiving the ball. The palm portion may be faced with 
crepe rubber or ping-pong rubber sheeting. The thickness of facing in case of crepe rubber shall be 
between 1 '3 to 1 '6 mm and ping-pong rubber V5 to 2 mm. 

6. Marking — Each glove shall be legibly and indelibly marked on the inside of the wrist with the 
manufacturer's name, initials or registered trade-mark. 

6.1 IS! Certification Marking ~~ Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

7. Packing — Wicket keeping gloves shall be kept in pairs and tied with twine and packed in accord- 
ance with best trade practice or according to the instructions of the purchaser. 



8. Sampling — Sampling and criteria for acceptance for vyicket keeping gloves shall be as agreed to 
between the purchaser and the supplier, A recommended scheme for the same is given in Appendix A. 



IS : 3785-1983 



APPENDIX A 

( Clause 8 ) 

RECOMMENDED SAMPLING SCHEME AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 

FOR WICKET KEEPING GLOVES

materials shall be grouped together to constitute a lot-

lot shall be in accordance with col 1 and 2 of i able 2.

A-3. NiUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 

A-3.1 Each pair of wicket keeping gloves selected in accordance with A-2.1 and Table 2, shall be 
inspected for all the requirements of materials, manufacture and dimensions. A pair shall be consider- 
ed as defective if it fails to satisfy any one or more of the requirements. The lot shall be declared as 
conforming to the requirements of this specification if the num.ber of defective pairs in the sample does 
not exceed the corresponding permissible number of defective pairs given in col 3 of Table 2. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was first prepared in 1966. The present revision has been taken up to incorporate 
certain modifications brought to the notice of the Sectional Committee due to the experience gained 
during the last few years while implementing this standard.
